"""Shared client for the internal Pipelines API v2.

This module is vendored into several repositories; it depends only on the
standard library and exposes a single class, :class:`PipelinesClient`.

Authentication
--------------
Requests carry ``Authorization: Bearer <token>``. The token is read from the
``PIPELINES_TOKEN`` environment variable unless passed explicitly; the client
fails fast at construction time if no token is available. A 401 response
means the token is missing, malformed or expired (tokens live 12 hours): the
client raises immediately and never retries a 401.

Rate limits
-----------
Each token may make 20 requests per second. On 429 the client waits the
number of seconds given by the ``Retry-After`` header and retries, at most 3
times, before raising :class:`PipelinesError` with code ``rate_limited``.
Respecting ``Retry-After`` is not optional: the API sits behind a shared
gateway and one script ignoring it throttles the whole team.

Other retried statuses (see docs/errors.md): 500 is retried once after
2 seconds; 503 is retried with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s), at most
3 times. All other error statuses are raised immediately.

Errors
------
API errors raise :class:`PipelinesError`, which carries the machine-readable
``code`` from the error envelope (branch on this, never on ``message``), the
HTTP ``status``, and the ``X-Request-Id`` header value as ``request_id`` --
support cannot trace a failure without it, so always include it in tickets.

Example
-------
    from client import PipelinesClient, PipelinesError

    client = PipelinesClient()
    try:
        run = client.start_run("p_17", "release/2.4", {"env": "prod", "shards": 8})
        final = client.wait_for_run(run["run_id"], timeout_s=45 * 60)
    except TimeoutError:
        client.cancel_run(run["run_id"])  # run_finished is treated as success
        raise SystemExit(1)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from typing import Any, Optional

__all__ = ["PipelinesClient", "PipelinesError"]

BASE_URL = "https://pipelines.example.internal"
TOKEN_ENV_VAR = "PIPELINES_TOKEN"

#: Run statuses after which the run will never change again.
TERMINAL_STATUSES = frozenset({"succeeded", "failed", "cancelled"})

POLL_INTERVAL_S = 2.0
MAX_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES = 3
MAX_UNAVAILABLE_RETRIES = 3
INTERNAL_ERROR_RETRY_DELAY_S = 2.0
DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0
PER_PAGE = 100  # API maximum; larger values are rejected with invalid_request.

# Expected caller action per error code, from docs/errors.md. Surfaced in
# str(PipelinesError) so callers can decide what to do without reading
# either this file or the docs.
_CALLER_ACTIONS = {
    "invalid_request": "fix the request; never retry unchanged",
    "unauthenticated": "refresh the token; do not retry with the same token",
    "forbidden": "do not retry",
    "not_found": "do not retry",
    "run_finished": "treat as success if the goal was to stop the run",
    "name_taken": "choose another name",
    "rate_limited": "wait Retry-After seconds, then retry, at most 3 times",
    "internal": "retry once after 2 seconds, then give up",
    "unavailable": "retry with backoff, at most 3 times",
}


class PipelinesError(Exception):
    """Error returned by the Pipelines API (or a transport-level failure).

    Attributes:
        code: Machine-readable error code from the API's error envelope,
            e.g. ``name_taken`` or ``rate_limited``. Programs must branch on
            this attribute, never on ``message``. Transport failures use the
            synthetic code ``connection_error``.
        message: Human-readable description from the API; may change.
        status: HTTP status code, or None for transport-level failures.
        request_id: Value of the ``X-Request-Id`` response header. Include it
            in any support ticket; support cannot trace a failure without it.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        code: str,
        message: str,
        status: Optional[int] = None,
        request_id: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.code = code
        self.message = message
        self.status = status
        self.request_id = request_id
        super().__init__(code, message)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        text = f"{self.code}: {self.message}"
        details = []
        if self.status is not None:
            details.append(f"HTTP {self.status}")
        if self.request_id:
            details.append(f"request_id={self.request_id}")
        action = _CALLER_ACTIONS.get(self.code)
        if action:
            details.append(f"caller action: {action}")
        if details:
            text += " (" + "; ".join(details) + ")"
        return text


class PipelinesClient:
    """Client for the Pipelines API v2.

    Args:
        token: Bearer token. Defaults to the ``PIPELINES_TOKEN`` environment
            variable.
        base_url: API base URL; override only for testing.
        timeout_s: Per-request socket timeout in seconds.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no token is provided and ``PIPELINES_TOKEN`` is unset.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        token: Optional[str] = None,
        base_url: str = BASE_URL,
        timeout_s: float = DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S,
    ) -> None:
        if token is None:
            token = os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV_VAR)
        if not token:
            raise ValueError(
                "no Pipelines API token: pass token=... or set the "
                f"{TOKEN_ENV_VAR} environment variable"
            )
        self._token = token
        self._base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self._timeout_s = timeout_s

    def list_projects(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Return every project, following pagination to the last page.

        Pages of 100 (the API maximum) are requested until the API's
        ``next_page`` field is null. The result is always complete: a page
        that still fails after the allowed retries raises
        :class:`PipelinesError` instead of silently returning a partial list.

        Returns:
            A list of project objects, e.g.
            ``{"id": "p_17", "name": "ingest", "visibility": "internal"}``.

        Raises:
            PipelinesError: If any page request fails.
        """
        return self._list_paginated("/v2/projects")

    def list_runs(self, project_id: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Return every run of a project, newest first, across all pages.

        Same pagination contract as :meth:`list_projects`.

        Args:
            project_id: The project id, e.g. ``"p_17"``.

        Returns:
            A list of run objects (see :meth:`get_run` for the shape).

        Raises:
            PipelinesError: With code ``not_found`` if the project does not
                exist or is not visible to the token, or if any page fails.
        """
        return self._list_paginated(f"/v2/projects/{project_id}/runs")

    def create_project(self, name: str, visibility: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Create a project.

        Args:
            name: Project name.
            visibility: ``"private"`` or ``"internal"``.

        Returns:
            The created project object.

        Raises:
            PipelinesError: With code ``name_taken`` if a project with this
                name already exists (branch on ``exc.code`` to retry with a
                suffixed name), or ``invalid_request`` if the body fails
                validation.
        """
        return self._request(
            "POST",
            "/v2/projects",
            body={"name": name, "visibility": visibility},
            expected=(201,),
        )

    def start_run(
        self, project_id: str, ref: str, params: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Start a run on a project.

        Args:
            project_id: The project id, e.g. ``"p_17"``.
            ref: The git ref to run, e.g. ``"release/2.4"``.
            params: Run parameters, e.g. ``{"env": "prod", "shards": 8}``.

        Returns:
            ``{"run_id": str, "status": "queued"}`` (API returns 202).

        Raises:
            PipelinesError: On validation or access errors.
        """
        return self._request(
            "POST",
            f"/v2/projects/{project_id}/runs",
            body={"ref": ref, "params": params},
            expected=(202,),
        )

    def get_run(self, run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Fetch the current state of a run.

        Args:
            run_id: The run id, e.g. ``"r_9f3a"``.

        Returns:
            The run object. ``status`` is one of ``queued``, ``running``,
            ``succeeded``, ``failed`` or ``cancelled``. Failed runs include a
            ``failure`` object with ``step`` and ``reason``.

        Raises:
            PipelinesError: With code ``not_found`` if the run does not exist.
        """
        return self._request("GET", f"/v2/runs/{run_id}")

    def cancel_run(self, run_id: str) -> Optional[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Cancel a run.

        A ``run_finished`` (409) response is *not* treated as an error: the
        run may have finished between the caller's last poll and this call,
        and the goal -- the run is stopped -- is met.

        Args:
            run_id: The run id, e.g. ``"r_9f3a"``.

        Returns:
            The response body on success, or None if the run was already in
            a terminal state.

        Raises:
            PipelinesError: For any error other than ``run_finished``.
        """
        try:
            return self._request("POST", f"/v2/runs/{run_id}/cancel")
        except PipelinesError as exc:
            if exc.code == "run_finished":
                return None
            raise

    def wait_for_run(self, run_id: str, timeout_s: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Poll a run every 2 seconds until it reaches a terminal status.

        Terminal statuses are ``succeeded``, ``failed`` and ``cancelled``.

        Args:
            run_id: The run id, e.g. ``"r_9f3a"``.
            timeout_s: Maximum time to wait in seconds.

        Returns:
            The final run object.

        Raises:
            TimeoutError: If the run is not finished when ``timeout_s``
                expires. Cancelling the run is the caller's decision; see
                :meth:`cancel_run`, which tolerates a run that finished in
                the meantime.
            PipelinesError: If a poll request fails.
        """
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
        while True:
            run = self.get_run(run_id)
            status = run.get("status")
            if status in TERMINAL_STATUSES:
                return run
            remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
            if remaining <= 0:
                raise TimeoutError(
                    f"run {run_id} still {status!r} after {timeout_s} seconds; "
                    "consider cancel_run() if it should not continue"
                )
            time.sleep(min(POLL_INTERVAL_S, remaining))

    def _list_paginated(self, path: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        items: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        page = 1
        while True:
            payload = self._request(
                "GET", path, query={"page": page, "per_page": PER_PAGE}
            )
            items.extend(payload.get("items", []))
            next_page = payload.get("next_page")
            # Stop when next_page is null, never on a short page.
            if next_page is None:
                return items
            page = next_page

    def _request(
        self,
        method: str,
        path: str,
        *,
        body: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
        expected: tuple[int, ...] = (200,),
        query: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
    ) -> Any:
        url = self._base_url + path
        if query:
            url += "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(query)
        headers = {
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {self._token}",
            "Accept": "application/json",
        }
        data = None
        if body is not None:
            data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
            headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"

        rate_limit_retries = 0
        unavailable_retries = 0
        internal_retried = False
        while True:
            request = urllib.request.Request(
                url, data=data, headers=headers, method=method
            )
            try:
                with urllib.request.urlopen(
                    request, timeout=self._timeout_s
                ) as response:
                    raw = response.read().decode("utf-8")
                    if response.status not in expected:
                        raise PipelinesError(
                            "unexpected_status",
                            f"expected HTTP {expected}, got {response.status}",
                            status=response.status,
                            request_id=response.headers.get("X-Request-Id"),
                        )
                    return json.loads(raw) if raw else {}
            except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
                # 429: wait the advertised delay and retry, at most 3 times.
                if exc.code == 429 and rate_limit_retries < MAX_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES:
                    rate_limit_retries += 1
                    time.sleep(_retry_after_seconds(exc.headers))
                    continue
                # 503: retry with backoff (2s, 4s, 8s), at most 3 times.
                if exc.code == 503 and unavailable_retries < MAX_UNAVAILABLE_RETRIES:
                    unavailable_retries += 1
                    time.sleep(2.0 ** unavailable_retries)
                    continue
                # 500: retry once after 2 seconds, then give up.
                # 401 and every other status: never retried.
                if exc.code == 500 and not internal_retried:
                    internal_retried = True
                    time.sleep(INTERNAL_ERROR_RETRY_DELAY_S)
                    continue
                raise _api_error(exc) from exc
            except urllib.error.URLError as exc:
                raise PipelinesError(
                    "connection_error",
                    f"could not reach {self._base_url}: {exc.reason}",
                ) from exc


def _retry_after_seconds(headers: Any) -> float:
    """Parse the Retry-After header (seconds), defaulting to 1s."""
    value = headers.get("Retry-After") if headers else None
    try:
        return max(0.0, float(value))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return 1.0


def _api_error(exc: urllib.error.HTTPError) -> PipelinesError:
    """Build a PipelinesError from an HTTP error response."""
    request_id = exc.headers.get("X-Request-Id") if exc.headers else None
    try:
        payload = json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))
        error = payload["error"]
        code = error["code"]
        message = error["message"]
    except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError):
        code = f"http_{exc.code}"
        message = f"HTTP {exc.code} with an unreadable error body"
    return PipelinesError(code, message, status=exc.code, request_id=request_id)

def _api_error(self, exc, status, request_id):
    try:
        payload = json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))
        error = payload.get("error", {})
        code = error.get("code", f"http_{status}")
        message = error.get("message", exc.reason or "")
    except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
        code, message = f"http_{status}", f"unreadable error body (HTTP {status})"
    return PipelinesError(code, message, status=status, request_id=request_id)
